environment.database: disposable synthetic SQLite, one recovery target and one isolation control

runs.transport: Owned ephemeral IPv4 loopback sockets, fixed FieldLog HTTP Host and Origin
Owned IPv4 loopback on port 8765 for account mode

observations: Strict apply, reverse, and reapply verified exact backend blobs.
The pinned ordinary account and static regression passed on both backends, including session capacity, confirmation, expiry, restart, and task and entry parity.

The CLI issued an expiring recovery code for an existing synthetic account. The service rejected replaced, replayed, and expired codes, invalid Origin, missing intent, incorrect callback binding, and cross-purpose exchange.
A forced SQLite session insert failure rolled back the proof change and revocations. The same approved exchange succeeded after removing the failure.
Recovery revoked existing confirmed and pending sessions and approved callbacks. Its new bearer required confirmation. The other account retained its grant.

Both callback registrations were exercised over HTTP. Lost browser, exchange, and confirmation responses recovered through a fresh recovery attempt, ordinary sign-in with the staged proof, and repeated confirmation respectively.
The complete task, task event, entry event, and photo rows matched their pre-recovery snapshots. Account and scope IDs matched and foreign keys checked cleanly.
limitations: One initial fixed-port run stopped at bind because port 8765 was already in use. Both documented replays later passed.
HTTP and SQLite evidence only. Root owns browser-to-native delivery and application composition.

independentRootReplay.scope: Independent source inspection and exact HTTP/SQLite replay. Native account recovery remains open.
